index.title: Home | tekstiks.ee
index.heroDescription: Automated speech transcription service for Estonian speech and a user interface for transcription editing.
index.tekstiksIntro: is a public speech recognition service of TalTech's Laboratory of Language Technology. The system demonstrates technologies and models developed in this lab. These currently achieve state-of-the-art Estonian speech recognition results, even compared to commercial alternatives. The system is fully automated and can process multiple files in parallel. There can be a queue and delays, especially during business hours. The average processing time is about half of the recording's length.
index.tekstiksIntroRemark: Coming soon: real-time progress and expected time of completion information
index.step1: 1. Upload a speech recording in Estonian
index.step1Desc: Most of the popular audio and video formats are supported. Max size limit is 500MB
index.step2: 2. Wait for the speech recognition to complete.
index.step2Desc: The system trained using machine learning methods will search for Estonian speech segments and tries to differentiate multiple speakers. Then it will transcribe the speech segments into text and finally will add punctuation. Many Estonain celebrities and radio personalities can be identified by name as well.
index.step3Desc: The editing of the transcription is interactive. The integrated audio player and the text are in sync. The currently playing word in coloured to simplify the manual editing.
index.step4Desc: Download the transcription, currently the DOCX format is supported.
index.rec1: The speech in the audio file should be of the best possible quality, i.e. recorded with a microphone near the mouth in a noise-free environment. The audio file should be at least 16-bit encoded and 16 KHz in frequency, preferably in WAV format.
index.rec2: As the maximum file size that can be uploaded is 500 MB, longer WAV files can be encoded in mp3 or ogg format, but it is recommended that you use at least 128 kbit encoding. Converting the stereo format to mono also saves volume (it is done anyway during detection).
index.rec3: The system does not work well with audio files longer than two hours. With such files, recognition may fail and the recognition result will not be returned. We recommend splitting long files first.
index.rec4: Due to limited resource of the recognition server, please do not upload more than 10 recordings per day. Otherwise, there will be a long queue in the system for all users. If you need to transcribe a large number of files (eg an entire audio archive), please contact us.
index.citing1: If you use this system for research, please refer to the article below in your publications (available at
index.osDesc: is based on freeware solutions that are easy to set up yourself. The recognition system can also be run from inside a Docker container (recommended).
index.osASR: Speech recognition system. It works as a step-by-step process that can be observed. Executable from the command line.
index.osServer: A web server solution that allows you to create a simple API through which to use speech recognition. Also supports returning of real-time processing progress information.
index.finnish1: Finnish speech recognition has been developed in co-operation with Finnish Language Bank and Aalto University. Speech recordings are processed by a service hosted by Finnish Language Bank.

terms.title: Terms of Use | tekstiks.ee
terms.h1: Terms of use of the service

blocks: Tekstiks.ee is a research and demonstration environment of the Laboratory of Language Technology at the Department of Software Science, Tallinn University of Technology, where you can use the laboratory's speech recognition software. The software is open source; anyone can install it themselves and use it in the same way.

The controller of personal data is Tallinn University of Technology (registry code 74000323, Ehitajate tee 5, 19086 Tallinn). The service is maintained and developed by Aivo Olev. Contact: konetuvastus@taltech.ee.

The service is intended for private individuals for personal use and for study and research. It is not intended for companies or organisations to process the personal data of clients, employees or other people in the course of their business or professional activities.

We do not enter into data processing agreements (Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR), do not guarantee uninterrupted operation of the service, and provide support on a best-effort basis.

If a recording contains people other than the user, the user is responsible for having the right to process the recording and for informing those people. The GDPR does not apply to processing carried out for purely personal or household purposes (Article 2(2)(c)); for any other purpose, the GDPR's requirements apply to the user.
Please do not upload recordings containing special categories of personal data (such as health data) unless you have a clear legal basis for doing so.

list: Account data: name, e-mail address, and either a password hash or a Google/Facebook account identifier and profile picture.
Sign-in data: the session's IP address and browser user agent.
Uploaded audio and video files, their names and durations, and transcripts including the user's corrections.

blocks: No analytics or advertising services that track user behaviour are used. If such services are introduced in the future, separate consent will be requested.

Data is processed to provide the service: to manage the account, transcribe recordings, and store files and transcripts so the user can keep working on them. The legal basis is the agreement with the user under these terms (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR).
If processing of a particular file fails, the service developer may view that file and its processing logs to find and fix the error. Otherwise, users' files are not opened.
Recordings and transcripts are not used to train speech recognition models or for any other purpose without the user's separate consent.

sections.h: Where data is processed and who receives it
blocks: Speech recognition, speaker diarization and punctuation of Estonian recordings, and storage of all files and transcripts, take place on servers managed by Tallinn University of Technology in Estonia. Data is not transferred outside the European Union.

list: For Finnish speech recognition, the audio file is sent to the speech recognition service of the Language Bank of Finland (Kielipankki) in Finland. The file name is replaced with a random identifier. The Language Bank's service does not store data long-term.

Notification and account e-mails are sent via the Microsoft 365 e-mail service. An e-mail contains the e-mail address and the message (for example the name of the transcribed file), but never recordings or transcripts.
When signing in with a Google or Facebook account, the respective provider processes the sign-in data.

blocks: Data is not disclosed or sold to any other third parties.
Files and transcripts are kept until the user deletes them.

When a file is deleted, the audio file, all its transcripts and other data related to the file are deleted immediately and permanently. Temporary processing data on the speech recognition servers is deleted within 24 hours after processing ends. No separate backups of users' files are made.
The account can be closed on the profile page. Closing the account deletes the account data and all of the account's files and transcripts.

You have the right to access, rectify and erase your personal data, to restrict or object to its processing, and to receive your data in a machine-readable format. You can delete your files and transcripts yourself; for anything else, write to konetuvastus@taltech.ee.
If you believe your personal data is processed unlawfully, you may lodge a complaint with the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate (www.aki.ee).
Users will be notified of material changes to these terms on the website or by e-mail before the changes take effect.

dictate.title: Dictate
dictate.intro1: This page allows you to dictate speech in multiple languages using TalTech realtime speech recognition. The web browser sends speech in real-time to the TalTech Laboratory of Language Technology server, where it is transformed into text and returned back to the browser.
dictate.intro3: For best results, use a good quality microphone and speak clearly at a moderate pace. You don't need to pause between words.
